jvAssociateProfit.title: Share of JV profit vs share of associate profit
jvAssociateProfit.content:
Power Assets holds no majority-controlled operating businesses of its own; almost everything is a joint venture (e.g. UK Power Networks until its H1 FY2026 sale, Australian Gas Networks) or an associate (e.g. HK Electric), equity-accounted. These two lines are its share of their profit under the equity method — earnings recognised, whether or not distributed as cash.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: this is the closest equivalent to an operating income statement this holding company has; the consolidated Revenue/NetIncome lines mix in items (loan interest, disposal gains) that obscure it.

What to watch:

  • JV profit falling as UKPN drops out of the portfolio post-sale
  • Associate profit (HK Electric) as the more stable, regulated counterweight
  • The gap between profit recognised here and cash actually received (see the cash-received chart)

cashReceived.title: Cash received vs statutory revenue
cashReceived.content:
Statutory Revenue on this dashboard is almost entirely shareholder-loan interest from JVs/associates and excludes their dividends entirely — it understates the cash the parent actually receives by roughly 85%. The bars here are the components the DCF is built on: JV dividends, associate dividends, associate distributions and loan interest, summed (plus treasury interest, not charted) into the DCF's base cash flow.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: value the cash-received bars, not the statutory revenue line — the DCF JSON's inputs.base_revenue_basis field spells out the exact FY2025 arithmetic (dividends 2,958 JV + 1,423 associate, loan interest 722, treasury interest 105 = 5,208).

What to watch:

  • Loan interest income has been declining since FY2017 as JVs pay down parent loans — a genuine mild headwind, not noise
  • Whether dividend growth offsets that decline
  • UKPN's cash contribution disappearing from FY2026 onward following its sale

ukpnDisposal.title: UK Power Networks disposal gain (one-off)
ukpnDisposal.content:
Power Assets sold its UK Power Networks joint-venture stake in H1 FY2026, booking a gain of roughly HK$11.3bn — large enough on its own to more than double reported net income for the period.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: this gain is a one-off realisation of value already reflected in the JV's book/fair value, not a repeatable earnings event, and it is explicitly excluded from the DCF's base cash flow (inputs.base_revenue_basis in the DCF JSON).

What to watch:

  • Net income excluding the gain when judging run-rate profitability
  • How the ~HK$42.5bn net cash position it helped create (see the equity bridge) gets deployed — reinvestment vs special dividend
  • The loss of UKPN's JV profit and dividend contribution in future periods

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF here is a parent-only operating cash flow line less minimal parent capex — it is small and not very meaningful on its own.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: this is an investment holding company with no consolidated operations of its own. Its real cash-generative engine is JV/associate dividends, distributions and shareholder-loan interest (see the JV & Associate Portfolio section below), which is what the DCF is actually built on — not this chart.

What to watch:

  • Use the Cash Received chart in the JV & Associate Portfolio section instead of this one to judge distributable cash
  • Net income here includes equity-accounted JV/associate profit that may not have been received as cash, plus one-offs like the FY2026 UKPN disposal gain

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue here is almost entirely shareholder-loan interest earned from JVs/associates — it is not a conventional sales line, because Power Assets has no significant consolidated trading operations of its own.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: this line excludes JV and associate dividends entirely and understates the cash actually received by roughly 85%. The DCF's base cash flow is built from the Cash Received chart in the JV & Associate Portfolio section, not from this line.

What to watch:

  • Do not compare this YoY growth rate with the DCF's growth path — they are different series
  • Declining loan interest as JVs pay down parent loans over time

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Power Assets Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
